content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem's symptom line, aiming for something like "Shoppers' account pages failed to load" and noting it should not include an impact figure. I'm also starting the causal chain, with the first step tying the failed account page requests to the errors cited in Gbac1 and G5309.

Next I'm laying out the causal chain's middle links: the ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, then the monthly-spend flag switched on at P1, which I'm tying to the error onset at 02:14. I'm also ruling out P2, since it landed at 02:20, after the errors began.

I'm checking the postmortem's causal chain against the evidence, and the flag-to-error link holds up. I'm noting that the divide-by-zero mechanism for shoppers with no purchases this month rests on F1 alone, since no other row confirms it, and I'm marking that as an unrun reading. I'm also starting the contributing factors section with the lack of a check before the flag was switched on.

I'm settling on the contributing factors now: the missing check before the flag went on is the first, since nothing in the record shows a test that exercised the flagged path for shoppers with no purchases this month. I'm proposing an item that requires flag changes to pass tests on the flag-on path before they are switched on in production. I'm also looking at the rollout, since the flag appears to have gone to all traffic at once, with no gradual step or automatic halt visible.

I'm weighing whether the third contributing factor, that nobody was paged, actually shortened the incident, since Argus mitigated it anyway, and I'm considering whether it belongs as a went-wrong item instead of a contributing factor.

I'm deciding that the "went wrong" item about nobody being paged belongs with the detection actions, not the contributing factors, since Argus mitigated the incident anyway. I'm also considering whether account pages should render without the spend summary when it errors, since the record shows one failing computation failing the whole request.

I'm weighing whether to note that the faulty function still raises for shoppers with no purchases at all, which would mean switching the flag back on would bring the account-page failures back.

I'm drafting the action items now: a pre-switch-on check requiring the flag-on path to pass tests, a gradual rollout with an automatic halt on rising error rates, and making the account page render without the spend summary when it fails. I'm also noting that routing the HighErrorRate alert to on-call paging doesn't answer any contributing factor.

I'm listing the lessons for the went-well section: the Investigator Agent tying the onset to the flag switch-on, the Mitigation Agent reverting the flag, Argus finding the second change P2 in the flag provider's history, and the Code-Fix Agent proposing draft PR #530. I'm also noting that nobody was paged, since the alert was linked to no on-call incident.

I'm checking the went-wrong list and the lessons, and I'm noting that I may be leaving out the window that ended at 02:15 as a finding. I'm also weighing whether the assumptions note should say that the empty this-month list mechanism rests on Code-Fix's reading, since nothing ran to confirm it.

I'm settling the plain-language cause: the feature switch sent account pages through a spend-per-item calculation that likely divides by zero for shoppers with no purchases this month, so their pages failed.

I'm placing the chain's third step at the moment the flag was switched on, and I'm keeping the symptom and first step free of impact figures. For the ruled-out case, P2 landed after the errors began, and the service recovered with P2 still on once only the monthly-spend flag had been reverted, so P2 doesn't account for the failures.

I'm deciding whether to keep the claim about P2 simple: it came after the onset, so I'll cite the timing and the errors it doesn't line up with, without adding anything beyond that. I'm also avoiding any specific clock times or counts for the errors, and I'm dropping the "day before" wording in favor of just saying the window that was read.

I'm checking the root-cause wording, making sure the function name, file path, and the division-by-zero mechanism are described as the evidence supports, without repeating the line number.

I'm wording the root cause to name the function and file, and noting that the zero count comes from a shopper with no purchases this month. I'm also marking the "had it been otherwise" check as next.

action_items.item: Require tests that run a feature flag's on path to pass before that flag can be switched on in production for io-shop.
Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop to a small share of traffic first, and stop the rollout automatically when the error rate rises.
Make the account page load without the spend summary when the summary fails, rather than failing the whole request.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person is paged when it fires.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until a fix for the spend summary is merged and deployed.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed with errors, and the account page error rate stayed high minute after minute.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.

ruled_out.what: The switch-on of the flag an-unrelated-feature at {P2.1}. It came after the onset at {T6.2}, by which time the account page errors were already high.
A deploy. The read of production changes found no deploy.

causal_chain.step: At {P1.1} the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Before that, its evaluations came back all off. In the minute it was switched they were split, and after that they were all on. The division-by-zero errors began in the minute the flag was switched.
With the flag on, the account page divides the month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought nothing this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a feature switch made shoppers' account pages work out their average spend per item this month, and that sum fails by dividing by zero, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off for all evaluations to on for all evaluations straight away. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers, and nothing that stops a rollout on rising errors, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failing path, and the rollout could have been stopped before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: An error while working out the spend summary failed the whole account page request rather than only leaving out that figure.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Shoppers would still have got their account pages, just without the monthly spend figure, even with the division by zero still in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent named the switch-on of monthly-spend-feature as the leading candidate cause.
Argus read the flag provider's history beyond the window the investigation had read, and found the later switch-on of an-unrelated-feature.
The Mitigation Agent turned monthly-spend-feature off, which can be undone.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #530.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called to the incident.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend figure goes through average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month and has no case for a shopper who bought nothing this month. For such a shopper the number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again before a fix is in place, account pages could fail again, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
